name: Phinehas
source_summary: Younger son of Eli the priest, who along with his brother Hophni abused his priestly office at Shiloh, was warned of coming judgment, and died in battle the same day the Philistines captured the ark of the covenant.
family_friendly_summary: Phinehas was one of Eli the priest's two sons who served at the tabernacle in Shiloh. Unlike his righteous ancestor who shared his name, this Phinehas and his brother Hophni did not honor God in their roles as priests -- they treated the offerings brought to God with disrespect and lived in ways that dishonored their position. A man of God warned Eli that judgment was coming because he had not stopped his sons. Later, when Israel took the ark of the covenant into battle against the Philistines hoping it would guarantee victory, Israel lost badly, the ark was captured, and both Phinehas and Hophni were killed the same day, just as had been warned.
adult_story: Phinehas, younger son of Eli the priest at Shiloh, served alongside his brother Hophni, but Scripture bluntly calls them 'worthless men' who 'did not know the LORD' (1 Samuel 2:12). They took meat from worshipers' sacrifices by force before it was properly offered, treating the LORD's offering 'with contempt,' and Phinehas is separately implicated, with his brother, in sexual immorality with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting (2:13-17, 22). Eli rebuked them, but they ignored him, and an unnamed man of God warned Eli that both his sons would die on the same day as a sign of coming judgment on his house (2:27-34). That judgment fell when Israel, losing a battle against the Philistines, brought the ark of the covenant into camp as a talisman for victory; instead, Israel was routed, the ark was captured, and Hophni and Phinehas both died in the defeat (4:3-11). Phinehas's pregnant wife, hearing the news of the ark's capture and her husband's and father-in-law's deaths, went into labor and died giving birth, naming her son Ichabod -- 'the glory has departed' -- because the ark, the visible sign of God's presence, was gone from Israel (4:19-22). Phinehas's account is a sobering warning that holding a priestly office does not itself guarantee reverence for God, and no religious symbol can substitute for genuine covenant faithfulness.

devotionals: Phinehas held a priest's office but treated God's offerings and God's house with contempt. Jesus is the priest who always honors God perfectly on our behalf.
The ark's capture taught Israel that no religious symbol can replace real faithfulness to God. Jesus Himself, not any object, is where God's presence now dwells with us.
